messages:
maria.g: Heads up — after the autotuner change landed last night I'm seeing a ~10-15% p95 latency regression on some workloads. Only reproduces on a narrow band: seqlen 96-256, batch 4-8, and models with head_dim around 20-28. No regression on short or very long sequences.

devon: hmm, narrow seqlen window + specific head_dim smells like kernel selection flip. Can you paste the kernel pick logs and a repro? :eyes:

maria.g: repro script attached (quick gist): https://gist.github.com/xxx - run with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 and AUTOTUNE_LOG=1. Kernel pick log snippet: 
```
[autotune] model=redwood/xx type=causal seqlen=128 headdim=24 batch=4 -> selected: flash_v2_tile_causal kernel (est cost 12.4ms)
[autotune] fallback candidate: sdpa_v3_prefetch (est cost 10.1ms)
```
But runtime is actually slower when flash_v2 gets chosen (p95 18.2ms vs sdpa_v3 ~15.8ms).

liam: can you grab a quick nvprof / nsight sample? If the flash path is thrashing memory we might be hitting lower L2 reuse which explains the perf delta. Also want to see warmup behavior (first 10 tokens).

maria.g: attached short perf dump from the run (trimmed): 
```
seqlen=128 headdim=24 batch=4
kernel=flash_v2_tile_causal: SM% 72, L2_BW 120GB/s, L2_HIT 24% 
kernel=sdpa_v3_prefetch: SM% 65, L2_BW 160GB/s, L2_HIT 41%
latencies: flash_v2 p50=8.1 p95=18.2, sdpa_v3 p50=7.9 p95=15.8
```
Looks like sdpa_v3 gets better L2 locality.

devon: interesting — autotuner cost model underestimated memory-bandwidth effects for that headdim. Could be the prefetch margin or tile size heuristic that's tuned for multiples of 32 heads. head_dim~24 falls into an awkward partial-tile case.

sam: +1. I can add a quick guard to prefer sdpa_v3 when headdim % 8 != 0 or when seqlen in [64,256] until we fix the estimator. That would be a config flag flip. Want a quick rollback?

maria.g: rollback would be safest for customer-facing pools. For dedicated infra we can flip per-pool. I put a small reproducer under: https://ci.internal/repro/2801234567 — uses real traces.

liam: another datapoint: on sm90 nodes we saw prefetch micro-bubbles when head_dim not aligned to warp lanes; prefetcher issues cause extra global loads. Maybe the flash kernel's prefetch schedule is too aggressive and evicts KV cache lines.

oncall: pinged oncall for impact assessment. Is this triggering any errors or just perf?

maria.g: only perf regression so far, no errors. Some customer synthetic tests show increased P99 tail on chat endpoints (low volume but latency sensitive).

devon: plan: 1) flip autotune to favor sdpa_v3 for the observed region (quick config change) 2) add microbench harness that sweeps headdim in [16..64] for seqlen buckets 3) instrument autotuner to include L2_estimate and mem-bandwidth term. Sam can you own 1? Liam own 2? Maria to file bug and collect traces.

sam: got it — will open hotfix PR and config toggle. Will also add a rollout plan (canary on non-prod then ramp).

liam: I'll script the sweep and add a perf job for the nightly matrix. Also will dump per-kernel L2 metrics so autotuner can ingest them.

maria.g: filed bug: https://internal/issue/RI-3245 with traces + repro. Adding short checklist in the issue: repro, nvprof traces, kernel logs, quick rollback PR id.

infra-bot: deploys: none in progress targeting inference-autotuner in last 24h. Notified owners.

devon: leaving a note — when we tune the autotuner cost function remember to penalize kernels that cause >20% L2 eviction rate when there is active KV caching (we want to avoid thrashing).

sam: PR opened: https://git.internal/repo/pulls/789 (hotfix toggle + tests). Rolling canary to staging now. :zap:

maria.g: thanks — will watch staging metrics and post a summary in the issue. If anyone hits different head_dim breakpoints, drop the quick perf output here.

devon: after canary and sweep we should add a unit in the autotuner that does a cheap simulated L2 reuse calc for partial tiles, saves us from these surprises.
